paper.title: Variance-Aware Non-Stationary Bandits:All-Budget Regret Bounds and Adaptation Costs

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic non-stationary bandits with supplied variation budget B (class D(A,T,B))
unmapped: Rewards are deterministic arrays in [0,1]; the learner knows the promise of determinism
Variation budget B bounds sum_t ||mu_t - mu_{t-1}||_inf excluding the initial vector (mapped to V_T)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal D(A,T,B)$ contain all deterministic reward arrays in $[0,1]^{T\times A}$ with $\Delta\le B$. The learner knows $A,T,B$ and the promise of determinism, but not the initial reward vector.

settings.name_in_paper: Noisy non-stationary bandits with supplied variance envelope Q and variation budget B (class E(A,T;Q,B))
unmapped: The learner knows a bound Q on the variance envelope sum_t max_a sigma_{t,a}^2 (symbol Q_env)
Variation budget B bounds sum_t ||mu_t - mu_{t-1}||_inf excluding the initial vector (mapped to V_T)
Oblivious environment fixes time-varying reward laws on [0,1] in advance; variances may vary over time
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal E(A,T;Q,B)$ be the environments of Section~\ref{sec:model} satisfying $V_T\le Q$ and $\Delta\le B$. ... Here policies receive $A,T,Q,B$, but no individual reward variances, means, or change locations.

settings.name_in_paper: Disclosed deterministic one-improvement family (baseline nu^0_g and alternatives nu^{a,tau}_g)
unmapped: Learner knows the initial reward vector and the family description (baseline 1/2 on arm 1, 1/2-g on challengers; at most one challenger rises to 1/2+g from an unknown time)
Objective is a constrained frontier: worst-case one-change regret subject to a stationary-regret budget r on the baseline
settings.definition_quote: Fix $g\in(0,1/2]$. The stationary baseline $\nu^0_g$ has rewards $1/2$ on arm $1$ and $1/2-g$ on every challenger. For $a\ge2$ and $\tau\in\{2,\ldots,T\}$, the alternative $\nu^{a,\tau}_g$ changes only arm $a$ to $1/2+g$ from $\tau$ onward. ... All policies receive the initial vector and the family description.

unmapped: Learner knows initial vector and the single-pulse promise: one challenger has reward 1/2+g on an unknown interval [tau,rho)
Constrained frontier objective: worst-case pulse regret subject to stationary-regret budget r
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal H_g^{\rm pulse}$ contain the baseline and arrays in which one challenger has reward $1/2+g$ on $[\tau,\rho)$, where $2\le\tau<\rho\le T+1$, and has its baseline reward outside that interval. The initial vector and this single-pulse promise are disclosed.

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic non-stationary bandits without supplied variation budget (oracle-competitive ratio)
unmapped: Learner knows determinism of rewards but not the variation; performance measured as worst-case ratio of expected regret to the oracle rate Psi(A,T,Delta(mu))
settings.definition_quote: For a policy that receives no variation budget, define its worst-case ratio to the rate function in Theorem~\ref{thm:detminimax} by $\mathcal C(\pi;A,T)=\sup_{\mu\in[0,1]^{T\times A}} \frac{\E_\pi[R_T]}{\Psi(A,T,\Delta(\mu))}$. ... The policy knows the horizon and determinism but receives identical side information on all arrays.

algorithms.name: Safe calibration followed by clipped restarts (of Ito's hybrid algorithm)
Independent monitoring with a stationary-regret budget
Restarted hybrid algorithm of Ito (2021) at fixed period H

tuning: H = min{T, max{A, ceil(sqrt(kappa A T/(2B)))}}, kappa = min{1,4B}; H=T if B=0

source.label: thm:detminimax
source.quote: For every $A,T\ge2$ and $B\in[0,T-1]$, universal constants $c,C>0$ satisfy $c\Psi(A,T,B)\le\mathfrak R_{\rm det}(A,T,B)\le C\Psi(A,T,B)$. The upper bound is attained by a deterministic policy and holds pathwise.

results.notes: Paper's A is K and variation budget B mapped to V_T. Upper bound is pathwise (deterministic policy, deterministic rewards). Also the Q=0 branch of Theorem 4.1.

source.label: thm:detminimax
source.quote: For every $A,T\ge2$ and $B\in[0,T-1]$, universal constants $c,C>0$ satisfy $c\Psi(A,T,B)\le\mathfrak R_{\rm det}(A,T,B)$...

results.notes: Lower bound on minimax expected regret over randomized policies knowing A,T,B; proven in Appendix A via Lemma A.1 mixtures.

conditions: deterministic rewards with variation at most B

source.label: prop:filtered
source.quote: For any $H\in\{A,\ldots,T\}$, this policy satisfies $R_T\le A+\kappa A\left(\frac TH+1\right)+2HB.$

source.label: thm:jointminimax
source.quote: For every $A,T\ge2$, $Q\in[0,T/4]$ and $B\in[0,T-1]$, universal constants $c,C>0$ satisfy $c\Xi\le\mathfrak R(A,T;Q,B)\le C\log(AT)\,\Xi.$ If $Q=0$, the sharper upper bound $C\Xi$ holds without logarithms.

results.notes: Upper bound achieved by a combination of policies depending on branch (calibration+clipped restarts for 0<B<1, restarted Ito hybrid otherwise, Algorithm 1 for Q=0). Special cases B>=1 and B=0 given in eqs (matchedlarge),(matchedstationary). Q=0 case covered by r1.

source.label: thm:frontier
source.quote: For $T\ge16A$, $g\in(0,1/2]$, and $r\in[0,gT]$, universal constants $c,C>0$ satisfy $c\Phi_g(r)\le\mathfrak F_g(r)\le C\Phi_g(r)$, $\Phi_g(r)=\min\{gT,\;g\sqrt{nT}+\frac{g^2nT}{r+gn}\}$

results.notes: Worst-case one-change expected regret of Algorithm 3 while keeping baseline regret <= r.

results.notes: Lower frontier on worst-case one-change regret; class restricted by stationary budget.

source.label: cor:competitive
source.quote: If $T\ge16A$, every such policy satisfies $\mathcal C(\pi;A,T)\ge c(T/A)^{1/4}$ for a universal $c>0$. This is a lower bound on the competitive ratio; no matching unrestricted upper bound is claimed.

results.notes: Ratio of expected regret to the supplied-budget oracle rate; recorded as quantity other. Corollaries 5.3 and 5.4 give related qualitative impossibility statements (not recorded).

tuning: restart period H = min{T, ceil(max{1,(AQT/B^2)^{1/3}, sqrt(AT/B)})}; H=T if B=0

source.label: thm:noisyoracle
source.quote: there is a policy knowing $A,T,\delta,Q,B$ but no individual variances, means or change locations such that, on every environment with $V_T\le Q$ and $\Delta\le B$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_T\le\min\{T,\;C D_T(A+\sqrt{AQ}+(AQBT)^{1/3}+\sqrt{ABT})\}.$

results.notes: D_T = ell(1+log T), ell = log(64 A T^4/delta). Same rate as Corollary D.2 (oracle-tuned SEV-UCB), which it restates with the T cap.

symbols.Delta_var: actual total mean variation sum_{t>=2} ||mu_t - mu_{t-1}||_inf

source.label: thm:partition
source.quote: For the fixed-period policy in Algorithm~\ref{alg:sev}, $M=\lceil T/H\rceil$ and $\Reg_T\le C D_T(\sqrt{A\lceil T/H\rceil\Lambda_T}+A\lceil T/H\rceil+H\Delta).$

results.notes: Lambda_T is the selected-arm variance sum (canonical). Setting budgets not needed for this bound. Realized-regret version adds 4 sqrt(Lambda_T ell)+4 ell; general-partition version also stated.

tuning: fixed restart period H; fresh hybrid copy on blocks of length >= max{A,3}

source.label: prop:itoreduction
source.quote: Restarting the algorithm of \citet{ito2021hybrid} at fixed period $H$ gives $\E[R_T]=\widetilde O(\sqrt{A\lceil T/H\rceil Q}+A\lceil T/H\rceil+HB)$ on $\mathcal E(A,T;Q,B)$.

results.notes: Reduction derived in this paper from a prior static theorem; algorithm itself is prior work. With oracle tuning gives A+sqrt(AQ)+(AQBT)^{1/3}+sqrt(ABT) up to logs.
